tldr: Repeated fair Bernoulli assignments to fixed affine common-response blocks yield noiseless equations for a finite-population total effect. Theorem \(\mathrm{thm:proportional-underdetermined-surface}\) proves, for the declared fixed-map affine \(\ell_1\) class and only when \(p=d+1\), \(R\ge2\), and \(p/3\le R\le2p/3\), that a lawful preassignment Euclidean-ball converse and the finite pilot--holdout upper bound give \(Q(m,d,R)\asymp1/(mp)\) over all Borel original-record estimators. At \(R=\lfloor d/2\rfloor\), this yields a factor of order \(d\) improvement over every design-aware affine outcome rule. A polynomial obstruction at \(R=d\), followed by the source-dependent exponential upper at \(R=d+1\), proves a faster-than-polynomial one-record elbow. Separate theorems establish the one-record, two-unit, and square-and-tall regimes. The complete fixed-map precision surface and residual saturation law remain open, and no replay achievability result is claimed for the broader published class. The consumer is a prospective fair complete-block pooling benchmark for the original SNIPE authors\textquotesingle{} stable-map software replay.
